meta.note: Three of these four scenarios happened. The fourth did not and may never. Where a figure could not be verified from a real source it is held at zero and marked, rather than filled in with something plausible. A blank cell in a stress test is more honest than a confident guess, and you can see exactly which cells are blank.

scenarios.name: The 2008 crash
scenarios.summary: Shares around the world lost about two fifths of their value in twelve months. Bonds and gold went up. It is the classic example of why you own things that do not all move together.
scenarios.headline: From its top in October 2007 to its bottom in March 2009, the MSCI World index (a measure of shares in rich countries) fell 57.8 percent. That took seventeen months, not twelve, and it is the drop people really lived through.

scenarios.name: The Covid crash
scenarios.summary: Shares around the world lost a third of their value in twenty-three trading days, the fastest fall of that size on record. Then it all came back within months.
scenarios.headline: Shares around the world fell 34 percent in about five weeks, and the same index ended the year up 15.9 percent. Anyone who sold in March made the loss permanent and missed the recovery.

scenarios.name: The 1970s inflation shock
scenarios.summary: The case almost nobody tests for. Shares and bonds fell together while prices rose 22 percent. Gold nearly tripled. Spreading money across shares and bonds alone did not protect anyone.
scenarios.headline: Over two years, US shares lost 37 percent, or 49 percent once rising prices are counted. Bonds gained 5.7 percent, but lost about 13 percent once rising prices are counted. Both things a normal mix is made of failed at the same time.

scenarios.name: A reordering
scenarios.period: No period. This has not happened.
scenarios.summary: The United States loses its position at the centre of the financial system over a decade. The dollar falls hard, US assets de-rate, and capital moves toward Asia, the Gulf and elsewhere.
scenarios.headline: Every number in this scenario is an assumption, not a forecast. Nobody has data on a thing that has not occurred. Change the numbers and watch what happens: that is the entire point of this panel.
